label: diffuse; weakly copy-phase input q / output f
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps) and spread across all phases and token identities. The strongest activations (0.8-1.0 of max) are copy-phase steps whose input is q, and many involve q-f bigrams, but copy-phase q fires on only ~10% of its occurrences. Other enrichments are weak: original-phase t=2 (16% of mass, 1.8% rate), prev_tok i, first_tok i, late copy steps of long sequences, repeated input tokens (in_first=0). Never fires at t=0 and rarely at the delimiter. The best simple predicate (copy phase & (input q or output f)) reaches only F1 ~0.14 and mass recall ~0.31 on dev; no coherent per-step or history predicate tried captured it, so the activations likely depend on the hidden state in ways these variables do not describe.
